key_insight: EgoActionBench evaluates whether AI can break first-person videos of human manipulation into small, time-localized actions and identify which hand performs each action.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks offer limited support for evaluating fine-grained action descriptions, precise action timing, and associations between actions and the left hand, right hand, or both hands.
method: Introduce a benchmark for dense action captioning in egocentric human videos.
Represent continuous manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions.
Associate each action with the left hand, right hand, or both hands.
impact: The benchmark targets capabilities needed to learn embodied skills from human video: understanding exactly what happens, when it happens, and which hand is involved. The provided abstract is truncated, so benchmark scale and evaluation results are unavailable.
visual_elements: First-person video frame with left- and right-hand overlays.
Three-lane timeline for left-hand, right-hand, and two-handed actions.
Sequence diagram showing continuous manipulation split into atomic action captions.
Three icons highlighting action granularity, temporal precision, and hand association.
paper_title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
paper_authors: Yujiao Shen, Jiahe Song, Haitian Li, Jingkang Yang, Ziwei Liu
